faqs.a: They are complementary. Content-Security-Policy controls which resources load; Permissions-Policy controls which browser features (camera, geolocation, etc.) pages and iframes may use. Use both.

permissions-policy-generator.formula:
Permissions-Policy: directive=(allowlist), directive=(allowlist), ...

Allowlist forms:
  ()                       <- no one (deny)
  (self)                   <- this origin only
  (self "https://a.com")  <- this origin plus listed origins
  *                        <- every origin (avoid)

Example: camera=(), geolocation=(self), microphone=(self "https://meet.example.com")
howTo: Pick a preset: Strict denies everything, Balanced denies sensitive features and allows the rest on your own origin.
Fine-tune per directive with the chips: Unset (omit), Deny, Self, or Custom.
For Custom directives, enter the trusted origins once in the origins field (space or comma separated).
Copy the header value or download it as a text file.
Serve it as a real HTTP response header from your server or CDN — a <meta> tag will not work.
keyFacts: Permissions-Policy is an HTTP response header that controls which browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, and more) a page and its iframes may use.
Each directive takes an allowlist: () denies everyone, (self) allows only your own origin, and quoted origins add trusted third parties.
It replaces the older Feature-Policy header; modern browsers enforce Permissions-Policy natively.
Deny-by-default is the safe posture: allow a feature only where your site genuinely needs it.
Unlike Content-Security-Policy it cannot be set with a <meta> tag — it must arrive as an HTTP header.
Over-blocking breaks features silently (maps, video calls, payments), so test after tightening.

permissions-policy-generator.quickAnswer: The Permissions-Policy HTTP header controls which browser features your pages and embedded iframes may use. Each directive takes an allowlist: camera=() denies the camera to everyone, geolocation=(self) allows location only on your own origin, and microphone=(self "https://meet.example.com") adds a trusted third party. This generator builds the full header from simple per-directive toggles with Strict and Balanced presets.
permissions-policy-generator.tagline: Build a Permissions-Policy HTTP header from simple per-feature toggles.
permissions-policy-generator.workedExample:
Settings: camera set to Deny, geolocation set to Self, microphone set to Custom with trusted origin https://meet.example.com, everything else Unset.
Generated header:
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), geolocation=(self), microphone=(self "https://meet.example.com")
Reading: no page or iframe may touch the camera; geolocation works only on your own origin; the microphone works on your origin plus meet.example.com (for example an embedded video-call widget). Serve this as an HTTP response header — a <meta> tag will not work.
